**Installation:** `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muneebs/airlock/main/install.sh | bash`

## Highlights

- **Per-ticket sandboxes are actually provisioned.** `airlock sandbox <path-or-url>` created VMs that never ran provisioning — no `airlock` user, no Node runtime — leaving the worktree mount at `/home/airlock/projects/<name>` unreachable. The CLI and setup paths now funnel through the same `ProvisionSteps` builder, so the two can't drift apart again. (#14)
- **Remote sources clone inside the VM.** `gh:user/repo` and `https://` sources are cloned in the guest instead of on the host, so untrusted repository content never touches your filesystem. (#11)
- **Reverse-sshfs fallback.** When a virtiofs mount fails, the sandbox falls back to reverse-sshfs rather than coming up with a silently broken mount. (#12)
- **Concurrent `Create` is race-free.** Atomic name reservation for in-flight creates, `SandboxInfo.State` mutation moved under the mutex, and orphaned VMs cleaned up when `Start` fails. (#15)
- **Releases are immutable and attested.** Tags and assets are locked once published, and every archive carries build provenance signed by the workflow that produced it. (#18)

## Security / hardening

- **Immutable releases.** Once published, the tag can't be moved and assets can't be added, changed, or deleted — including if the repository is deleted and recreated.
- **Build provenance attestation.** Archives and `checksums.txt` are signed with a short-lived Sigstore certificate bound to the release workflow run. v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 were unsigned.
- **Base image pinned to a dated snapshot with a verified digest** (#13). The image previously floated, so two installs on different days could land on different base systems with no way to tell.
- **Remote clones happen in the guest, not the host** (#11). Untrusted repository content is never written to the host filesystem.
- **Unrecognized AI tools are surfaced instead of silently skipped** (#10). A typo'd `--ai-tool` used to provision a sandbox quietly missing the tool you asked for.
- **Concurrency correctness** (#15). The data race in `Create` surfaced under `go test -race` at tag time; the fix is verified under `-race` (67 tests in `internal/sandbox`).

## Known gaps

- CI does not yet run `go test -race`, which is why the concurrency bug above reached a tag before anything caught it.
- The CLI wiring that triggers provisioning has no automated regression guard — reverting it leaves the test suite green.
